trust_decision.summary: Whether a header name in a proxy's allow list may be filled with the client's emulation map is decided once per outgoing backend request: requestHeaders (HTTP) and requestMetadata (gRPC) copy the emulated map into the backend request whenever the name appears in the operator's transport allow list (http_headers/grpc_metadata), so at the pinned commit a client value is forwarded as if the edge had set it; the map itself is put into the connection context by OnClientConnecting.

landing_point.why: Grepping the advisory's terms (emulated headers / GetEmulatedHeadersFromContext) lands on this loop, the first place a client-supplied name is promoted into a backend request; the gRPC twin is ~50 lines away in the same package, while the app/config/client layers that decide whether the map exists at all are invisible from here.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The internal/app bookkeeping is only a retention optimisation: the spoofing decision is the two allow-list checks in requestHeaders/requestMetadata, so a solver can plausibly leave app/proxy.go and the connection-context gating alone and still claim the hole is closed ('the security fix is the two checks; the flag only avoids keeping an unused map').

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The emulated-header feature itself must keep working: a name listed in both lists is legitimate (browser sends Authorization via emulation, native client as a real header) and the transport value must win with the emulated value as fallback; and emulated headers captured at connect must keep reaching refresh/subscribe/publish/rpc proxies through the connection context. A fix that strips emulated headers outright passes the spoofing check but breaks both.

O6_input_shapes: mixed-case allow-list entry (config "X-App-Token") matched against the lowercased client name - needs normalisation of the new list, not just of http_headers
the same name in http_headers and emulated_headers (dual source): transport value preferred, emulated value used as fallback
emulated name present in neither allow list - dropped
a gRPC metadata key (lowercase) and a canonical HTTP header key reaching the same outgoing http.Header (duplicate-casing, so the transport value may not override the emulated one)
headers arriving at connect (per-call context) versus being replayed for later operations from the long-lived connection context

O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: a maintainer adding another client-visible source (connect-frame metadata promoted to HTTP headers, per-connection meta) would extend this exact function, and it must be classified trusted/untrusted like the other two

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a third transport's header builder (e.g. a WebTransport/HTTP3 or unidirectional backend) repeating the emulated/transport split
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: there are already two parallel builders that drifted on key casing (gRPC Set lowercases, the HTTP map assign does not), so any new transport becomes a third place the split must be repeated
